messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: multi-gpu collective anomaly detected
incident-bot: Alert id: 2026-03-15T10:34:59Z | severity: P1 | service: serving-runtime-tp | symptom: repeated NCCL communicator timeouts and GPU hangs on multiple pods in prod/us-west-2
elena: taking triage — who has console + gpu access? @samir?
elena: logs show `NCCL WARN Timeout waiting for response` and repeated `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` across TP workers
samir: on it, pulling node telemetry and kube events. pinging infra-sre for kernel dmesg
infra-sre: confirmed anomalies on gpu-node-42 and gpu-node-47 — nvlink resets and kubelet restarted containers on both nodes
ml-runtime: runtime traces show communicator split: `ncclCommConnect timed out` then `comm->state = NCCL_COMM_FAILURE` during rendezvous
elena: customer impact — chat-inference and embeddings-batch routes saw elevated 502/504s for brief windows (~1-3m each). Not a full region outage but meaningful error rate spike
customer-success: flagged one enterprise customer with SLA noise — ~10% request drop for ~5m, raising comms
samir: pulling logs from pod tp-worker-7: `kubectl -n prod logs tp-worker-7 -c runtime --since=15m`
samir: (excerpt pasted)
```
[10:31:14] NCCL WARN Retry 3: ncclCommInitRank failed, ret=2
[10:31:15] NCCL INFO NET/Plugin : Using ibv transport
[10:31:15] CUDA ERROR 77: Launch timeout
[10:31:16] ncclCommDestroy: communicators not synced
```
infra-sre: dmesg from gpu-node-42 shows Xid 79 events:
```
Mar 15 10:30:58 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 15 10:31:02 kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: CE severity corrected
```
elena: Xid 79 again — historically correlates to NVLink/driver flaps (firmware or hw)
ml-runtime: current topology is TP world_size=8 with shards pinned across nodes; single node drop causes NCCL rendezvous to hang waiting for all ranks
samir: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain & restart pods on healthy nodes 3) for critical routes, switch to single-GPU fallback model-var (lower perf but avoids TP fragility)
elena: I'll flip chat-inference to fallback model-v1-small now. Can oncall pause new TP submissions?
oncall-rotations: pausing TP scheduler for us-west-2 — ack
infra-sre: cordoning nodes gpu-node-42 and gpu-node-47 now
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force\```
samir: draining and recreating pods on gpu-node-39 and gpu-node-44
ml-runtime: applying route fallback (PATCH):
```
PATCH /routes/chat-inference
spec:
  model_priority: [model-v1-small, model-v2-large]
  fallback_policy: immediate
```
elena: applied. monitoring latency/errors closely
customer-success: notifying affected customer — ETA ~15m to steady state after failover applied
samir: one pod hitting CrashLoopBackOff on restart, logs show: `ncclCommInitRank failed: Daemon timed out waiting for peers` and container exit code 137
infra-sre: checking cgroup — appears OOM kill after big memory surge (pid 2145) during resync
ml-runtime: looks like KV cache resync pressure triggered memory spike, led to OOM -> container killed with half-formed communicator state
elena: short-term: reduce per-pod cache cap (KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES from 2GB -> 512MB) and canary redeploy to validate
samir: creating canary deployment tp-worker-canary with env overrides
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/tp-worker tp_role=canary KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=536870912
kubectl rollout status deploy/tp-worker-canary\```
elena: enabling NCCL debug on canary: NCCL_DEBUG=WARN,NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL and NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 to accelerate fail fast on peer faults
ml-runtime: after node cordon/drain + KV cache canary, error rate returned to baseline; chat-inference serving now on fallback with latency up ~120ms->240ms but 5xxs dropped
oncall-rotations: handoff to @jin in ~10m for next shift
elena: handing off to samir for RCA workstream; leaving notes in ticket INC-2026-0315-42
samir: collecting driver, kernel, firmware info — both nodes run nvidia-driver 525.105.17 and had a kernel patch applied 6 days ago; correlating timeline with past Xid79 incidents
infra-sre: opening vendor ticket and repro task tagged @nvidia-eng to validate NVLink/firmware stability
ml-runtime: longer-term runtime changes recommended: reduce rendezvous backoff (30s -> 8s), add aggressive communicator timeouts, and make single-GPU warm pools cheaper to switch to on faults
elena: agreed. create followup stories: RT-847 (faster failover), RT-848 (kv-cache mem throttle), INF-692 (firmware coord with vendor)
customer-success: customer updated — accepting interim mitigation, requested RCA when available
infra-sre: scheduling firmware+driver patch window tomorrow 03:00 UTC; will monitor post-upgrade
jin: taking over shift notes: canary with KV cache lowered, NCCL debug flags enabled, nodes cordoned. Watch alerts: serving-runtime-tp.ncc1.warn and kernel.XID79.rate
elena: incident state -> mitigated/monitoring. duration ~00:18:51. tagging INC-2026-0315-42. keep this channel for RCA followup
incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring | tickets: INC-2026-0315-42, TASK-rt-failover-042
elena: thanks team :thumbsup:
